userStories.title: Record escalation source tiers in telemetry
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make every newly emitted escalation observation auditable by logging the source rung and ensuring both escalation emitters are collected.

**Motivation** — Every escalation observation records an empty source tier, so the ladder cannot be audited.

**Approach** — Logger routed through `_tierEscalationDeps`; emits source tier. `collectObservations` is unchanged; the escalation entries it reads gain the missing field. Its private `collectEscalation` helper needs no change — it already falls back through `fromTier ?? from ?? currentTier`.

**Scope** — In: route `handleTierEscalation` logger resolution through `_tierEscalationDeps.getSafeLogger`; emit `fromTier` alongside the existing `nextTier`; align the pre-iteration escalation message with the collector’s case-sensitive `message.includes("Escalating")` dispatch; cover collector fallback inputs and entries from both emitters. Out: runtime-crash retry behavior (US-002); per-tier budget dispatch and defaults (US-003); Backfilling `payload.from` on escalation observations already written to disk by earlier runs.

**Interface** — Existing symbols this feature modifies — all verified present at the cited lines:

```typescript
handleTierEscalation(ctx: EscalationHandlerContext): Promise<EscalationHandlerResult>
collectObservations(context: CuratorPostRunContext): Promise<Observation[]>
```

**Design notes** — `_tierEscalationDeps` (`tier-escalation.ts:332`) already exports `savePRD` and `getSafeLogger`. `preIterationTierCheck:142` resolves its logger through it; `handleTierEscalation:343` calls the imported `getSafeLogger()` directly. That asymmetry is why the escalation log line is currently untestable, so US-001 routes `handleTierEscalation` through `_tierEscalationDeps.getSafeLogger` as well.
acceptanceCriteria: When `handleTierEscalation` emits an escalation log, then it obtains the logger through `_tierEscalationDeps.getSafeLogger` so a replacement dependency observes the call.
When `handleTierEscalation` escalates a story from `fast` to `balanced`, then it logs at stage `escalation` with `data.fromTier` equal to `"fast"`.
When `handleTierEscalation` escalates a story from `fast` to `balanced`, then the same escalation log has `data.nextTier` equal to `"balanced"`.

Given an escalation log entry with `fromTier: "fast"` and `nextTier: "balanced"`, when `collectObservations` reads the log, then it returns one `escalation` observation whose `payload.from` is `"fast"`.
Given an escalation log entry with `currentTier: "fast"` and no `fromTier`, when `collectObservations` reads the log, then it returns an observation whose `payload.from` is `"fast"`.
Given the log entry written by `handleTierEscalation` for an escalation, when `collectObservations` reads the log, then it returns exactly one observation of kind `escalation`.
Given the log entry written by `preIterationTierCheck` when a story exceeds its rung budget, when `collectObservations` reads the log, then it returns exactly one observation of kind `escalation`.
Given an escalation log entry, when `collectObservations` reads the log, then the returned observation has a non-empty string `payload.from`.

routing.reasoning: Touches an existing escalation emitter and collector dispatch using established dependency injection and structured-log conventions.

userStories.title: Retry runtime crashes on the current tier
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Translate the existing runtime-crash failure category into the existing same-tier escalation outcome and honor that outcome in the pipeline-result handler.

**Motivation** — Runtime crashes escalate to a costlier model tier instead of retrying the same one.

**Approach** — The crash signal is **not** given new plumbing. `tddFailureCategory === "runtime-crash"` already reaches the escalation call site, so `handlePipelineFailure` derives `runtimeCrashResult` from it rather than threading a parallel field from the verify layer. `shouldRetrySameTier`'s `{ status: "RUNTIME_CRASH" }` shape is preserved so the existing predicate and its tests stay valid.

**Scope** — In: derive `runtimeCrashResult` in the `escalate` branch from `pipelineResult.context.tddFailureCategory`; pass it to `handleTierEscalation`; read `EscalationHandlerResult.outcome` so `retry-same` returns the original PRD with `prdDirty: false`, unchanged tier, and unchanged attempts; preserve non-crash escalation. Out: source-tier telemetry emission and collector behavior (US-001); per-tier budget wiring and default changes (US-003); Provider capacity errors and transient adapter failures (BUG-62 / BUG-20) — a separate transient-failure taxonomy, not part of tier escalation.; Agent unavailability persisting for a whole run after one transient failure (BUG-52).

**Interface** — Existing symbols this feature modifies — all verified present at the cited lines:

```typescript
shouldRetrySameTier(runtimeCrashResult: { status: string; success: boolean } | undefined): boolean
handleTierEscalation(ctx: EscalationHandlerContext): Promise<EscalationHandlerResult>
```

**Failure handling** — Runtime crash detected | Same tier retried; story tier and `attempts` unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: When `shouldRetrySameTier` receives `{ status: "RUNTIME_CRASH" }`, then it returns `true`.
When `shouldRetrySameTier` receives `undefined`, then it returns `false`.
When `shouldRetrySameTier` receives `{ status: "TEST_FAILURE" }`, then it returns `false`.
When `handleTierEscalation` receives a context with a runtime-crash result, then it returns `outcome: "retry-same"`.
When `handleTierEscalation` returns `outcome: "retry-same"`, then it returns `prdDirty: false` and the unmodified PRD supplied in its context.
When `handleTierEscalation` receives a `tddFailureCategory` other than `"runtime-crash"`, then it returns `outcome: "escalated"` and advances the story `routing.modelTier` by one rung.

When `handlePipelineFailure` handles an `escalate` action whose `pipelineResult.context.tddFailureCategory` is `"runtime-crash"`, then it derives and passes a runtime-crash result to `handleTierEscalation`.
When `handlePipelineFailure` handles an `escalate` action for a runtime-crash failure, then the resulting story `routing.modelTier` is unchanged from before the call.
When `handlePipelineFailure` handles an `escalate` action for a runtime-crash failure, then the resulting story `attempts` is not reset to `0`.
When `handlePipelineFailure` handles an `escalate` action for a non-crash failure, then the resulting story `routing.modelTier` advances by one rung.

routing.reasoning: A clear two-module integration change must preserve a discriminated outcome and persisted story state.

userStories.title: Enforce per-tier attempt budgets before dispatch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Bind the configured per-rung attempt budget to sequential and batch execution while shipping the measured 2/2/2 default ladder.

**Motivation** — The per-tier attempt budgets in `autoMode.escalation.tierOrder` are never consulted, so the shipped ladder has never been in force or validated.

**Approach** — Budget enforcement reuses `preIterationTierCheck` as written — it already handles agent-qualified rungs, missing rungs, and the escalation-disabled case. This feature supplies callers, not a reimplementation.

**Scope** — In: change Zod schema defaults only from 5/3/2 to 2/2/2; add `preIterationTierCheck` to `_unifiedExecutorDeps`; invoke it before `runIteration` in sequential dispatch and once per story before batch dispatch; skip dispatch when its result has `shouldSkipIteration: true`; preserve resulting PRD state and existing dispatch semantics. Out: runtime-crash outcome plumbing (US-002); source-tier telemetry (US-001); Concurrent `savePRD` writes from simultaneous escalations in parallel/batch mode — the existing single-writer contract is unchanged by this feature.; `escalateEntireBatch` semantics — whether a batch escalates as a unit is unchanged.; `resetMode` semantics — how routing resets on escalation is unchanged.; Retuning the `2/2/2` budget values after measurement — this feature ships the corrected defaults, not a follow-up tuning pass.; US-003 only: retuning `maxIterations` or `execution.rectification.maxAttemptsTotal` to match the new per-rung budgets.

**Interface** — Existing symbols this feature modifies — all verified present at the cited lines:

```typescript
preIterationTierCheck(
  story: UserStory,
  routing: { modelTier: string },
  config: NaxConfig,
  prd: PRD,
  prdPath: string,
  featureDir: string | undefined,
  hooks: LoadedHooksConfig,
  feature: string,
  totalCost: number,
  workdir: string,
): Promise<PreIterationCheckResult>
calculateMaxIterations(tierOrder: TierConfig[]): number
```

**Design notes** — **Executor seam** — `_unifiedExecutorDeps.runIteration` (`unified-executor.ts:565`) is the established injection point for the sequential dispatch; the new pre-iteration call is added to the same deps object so tests can stub it without `mock.module()`. **Config defaults** — per `.nax/rules/config-patterns.md`, defaults live in the Zod schema and `DEFAULT_CONFIG` is derived via `NaxConfigSchema.parse({})`. Change the schema only.

**Failure handling** — Story's current rung absent from `tierOrder` | Budget is unbounded for that story; warn and proceed. `autoMode.escalation.enabled` is `false` | Budget exhaustion does not escalate; the iteration proceeds.
acceptanceCriteria: When `NaxConfigSchema.parse({})` is evaluated, then `autoMode.escalation.tierOrder` is `[fast, balanced, powerful]` with `attempts: 2` on every rung.
When `calculateMaxIterations` receives the default ladder, then it returns `6`.
When `preIterationTierCheck` receives a story with `attempts: 1` and a current-rung budget of `2`, then it returns `shouldSkipIteration: false`.
When `preIterationTierCheck` receives a story with `attempts: 2` and a current-rung budget of `2`, then it returns `shouldSkipIteration: true`.
When `preIterationTierCheck` returns `shouldSkipIteration: true` for an exhausted rung, then its returned PRD advances that story `routing.modelTier` to the next rung.
When `preIterationTierCheck` returns `shouldSkipIteration: true` for an exhausted rung, then its returned PRD resets that story `attempts` to `0`.
When `preIterationTierCheck` receives a story whose current tier is absent from `tierOrder`, then it returns `shouldSkipIteration: false` regardless of the story attempts value.
When `preIterationTierCheck` receives a story at its rung budget and `autoMode.escalation.enabled` is `false`, then it returns `shouldSkipIteration: false`.
When the sequential executor dispatches a selected story, then it invokes `preIterationTierCheck` once with that story before it invokes `runIteration`.
When the sequential executor receives `shouldSkipIteration: true` from `preIterationTierCheck`, then it does not invoke `runIteration` for that story.
When the batch executor dispatches a batch, then it invokes `preIterationTierCheck` once per batch story before the batch is dispatched.
When a story fails twice at the `fast` rung under the default ladder, then it reaches `balanced` and not `powerful`.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module execution scheduling changes sequential and batch control flow, persistent PRD transitions, dependency injection, and configuration defaults.

analysis: This is a TypeScript/Bun enhancement to the existing execution escalation path. The execution cluster owns tier transitions, persists PRD state through injectable savePRD seams, and emits structured logs consumed by the curator. `preIterationTierCheck` in src/execution/escalation/tier-escalation.ts:130 already resolves an injectable logger, evaluates an agent-qualified or tier-only rung through getTierConfig, warns and proceeds for an absent rung, escalates/reset-attempts when the current rung budget is exhausted, then saves the updated PRD. Graph analysis shows it has zero production callers, so the sequential and batch dispatches in src/execution/unified-executor.ts must call it before their respective iteration/batch execution paths and make it injectable via _unifiedExecutorDeps. `handleTierEscalation` in the same module (342-515) currently uses the imported getSafeLogger directly, returns the existing retry-same outcome when runtimeCrashResult has status RUNTIME_CRASH, then logs only nextTier while normal escalation is performed. `handlePipelineFailure` in src/execution/pipeline-result-handler.ts:279-392 is the sole direct caller: its escalate branch currently forwards PRD and prdDirty only, so it must derive runtimeCrashResult from pipelineResult.context.tddFailureCategory === "runtime-crash" and honor outcome to preserve tier/attempts on same-tier retries. The execution stage already classifies CALL_OP_NO_OUTPUT and CALL_OP_MAX_RETRIES as runtime-crash, so no parallel signal plumbing is required. `calculateMaxIterations` in src/execution/escalation/escalation.ts:66-68 remains a sum utility; the new default ladder is 2/2/2 and therefore sums to six, but the per-rung decision belongs exclusively to the pre-iteration check. `NaxConfigSchema` at src/config/schemas.ts:46-593 owns schema defaults; DEFAULT_CONFIG is derived from parsing this schema, so only its 5/3/2 ladder literals should change. The curator collector at src/plugins/builtin/curator/collect.ts:404-419 already maps fromTier, from, or currentTier into payload.from and nextTier into payload.to, but its stage/message dispatcher must recognize the pre-iteration warning's exact capitalization so it can create observations for both emitters. Existing tests are concentrated in test/unit/execution/escalation/tier-escalation.test.ts, test/unit/execution/escalation/escalation.test.ts, test/unit/config/schemas.test.ts, executor tests, pipeline-result-handler tests, and curator collection tests; expand those instead of creating isolated new abstractions. Risks are behavioral: an incorrect skip result can silently omit a scheduled iteration; accidental mutation on retry-same can reset attempts; and changing batch sequencing can alter existing batch semantics. Keep savePRD’s existing single-writer behavior, maintain agent-qualified rung matching, preserve the collector’s fallback chain, and test call ordering through the documented injectable seams. There is no config migration: user-provided tierOrder values retain their explicit values, while only empty-schema/default consumers receive 2/2/2. Historical observations are intentionally not rewritten.
outOfScope: Concurrent `savePRD` writes from simultaneous escalations in parallel/batch mode — the existing single-writer contract is unchanged by this feature.
`escalateEntireBatch` semantics — whether a batch escalates as a unit is unchanged.
`resetMode` semantics — how routing resets on escalation is unchanged.
Retuning the `2/2/2` budget values after measurement — this feature ships the corrected defaults, not a follow-up tuning pass.
Provider capacity errors and transient adapter failures (BUG-62 / BUG-20) — a separate transient-failure taxonomy, not part of tier escalation.
Agent unavailability persisting for a whole run after one transient failure (BUG-52).
Backfilling `payload.from` on escalation observations already written to disk by earlier runs.
US-003 only: retuning `maxIterations` or `execution.rectification.maxAttemptsTotal` to match the new per-rung budgets.
